inspiration.observed_pattern: A multi-stage CTE uses LAG to measure gaps, a running window SUM to assign contiguous groups, ordered GROUP_CONCAT plus COUNT(DISTINCT) to summarize each group, and HAVING predicates to recognize a repeated subject cycle.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a learner study-log report with independently named tables and rows. Explicit session identifiers make date ordering deterministic; gap-separated runs are summarized with ordered pipe-delimited subjects, rounded hours, distinct-subject cycle lengths, modulo divisibility, and repeated-prefix matching. The final join returns only qualifying learner runs with a stable tie-breaker.

fixture_notes: Learner 101 has one six-session ABC cycle and one qualifying report row; learner 102 repeats only AB and is excluded by the minimum cycle length; learner 103 has a non-divisible ABCABD sequence; learner 104 has two short runs split by a gap and is excluded; learner 105 has a valid six-session cycle with a lower total. Duplicate dates are avoided and session IDs provide a deterministic secondary order.
determinism_notes: All learner IDs, dates, session IDs, subjects, hours, grouping order, concatenation separator, rounding precision, and final ordering are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE learners (learner_id INT PRIMARY KEY, learner_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, major VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE study_logs (session_id INT PRIMARY KEY, learner_id INT NOT NULL, subject VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, session_date DATE NOT NULL, hours_studied DECIMAL(5,1) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: WITH gap_groups AS (SELECT sl.session_id, sl.learner_id, sl.subject, sl.session_date, sl.hours_studied, CASE WHEN DATEDIFF(sl.session_date, LAG(sl.session_date) OVER (PARTITION BY sl.learner_id ORDER BY sl.session_date, sl.session_id)) > 2 OR LAG(sl.session_date) OVER (PARTITION BY sl.learner_id ORDER BY sl.session_date, sl.session_id) IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS starts_group FROM study_logs AS sl), session_groups AS (SELECT gg.*, SUM(gg.starts_group) OVER (PARTITION BY gg.learner_id ORDER BY gg.session_date, gg.session_id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS group_id FROM gap_groups AS gg), pattern_groups AS (SELECT sg.learner_id, sg.group_id, GROUP_CONCAT(sg.subject ORDER BY sg.session_date, sg.session_id SEPARATOR '|') AS subject_sequence, COUNT(*) AS total_sessions, COUNT(DISTINCT sg.subject) AS cycle_length, ROUND(SUM(sg.hours_studied), 1) AS total_study_hours FROM session_groups AS sg GROUP BY sg.learner_id, sg.group_id HAVING total_sessions >= 6 AND cycle_length >= 3 AND total_sessions % cycle_length = 0 AND REPEAT(CONCAT(SUBSTRING_INDEX(subject_sequence, '|', cycle_length), '|'), total_sessions / cycle_length) = CONCAT(subject_sequence, '|')) SELECT pg.learner_id, l.learner_name, l.major, pg.cycle_length, pg.total_study_hours FROM pattern_groups AS pg INNER JOIN learners AS l ON l.learner_id = pg.learner_id ORDER BY pg.cycle_length DESC, pg.total_study_hours DESC, pg.learner_id

checks.sql: SELECT learner_id, COUNT(*) AS sessions FROM study_logs GROUP BY learner_id ORDER BY learner_id
